newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas holds gains late on firmer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas holds gains late on firmer cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures held modest gains late Wednesday in sluggish trade, helped by reports of firmer physical prices and some short covering after the recent 10 percent slide, market sources said.
At 1400 EDT, July was still up by 5.2 cents at $2.155 per million British thermal units, while August was 4.7 cents higher at $2.17. Other months also were holding modest gains.

"The weather hasn't helped lately, but I don't think we'll see any material moves down anymore. I think we're setting up for a new and higher trading range," said one New York futures trader, adding any move lower may be a buying opportunity.
With forecasts next week calling for more heat in the Southwest and California and some above-normal weather in Texas and the South, some traders agreed the near-term bottom may be in place.
"I think there are some size buyers below and $2.09 (basis July) will be a hard number to break," said an East Coast trader, adding there was more upside than downside potential from here.
But with temperatures in the Midwest and East expected to range from normal to below-normal next week, few expected the market to break to new highs.
Traders saw little impact from tonight's weekly AGA storage data, with most expecting a build in the 80-85 bcf range versus an 88-bcf gain last year.

Technical traders differed on whether the near-term low was in place after the four-day, 10 percent selloff. July support was pegged at yesterday's low of $2.08 and then at $2.05 and $2.00. Resistance was seen at $2.21, $2.25, $2.37-2.38 and the contract high of $2.44.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed Wednesday by more than five cents to the mid-teens. Midcon pipes were several cents higher in the low-$2s. New York city gate prices gained a few cents to about $2.40.
NYMEX said 19,329 contracts traded at 1340 EDT. Hub open interest on June 3 fell 2,251 contracts to 194,001.
On the KCBT, July firmed 4.8 cents to $2.01, while deferreds were still steady to six cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 0.4 cent to 14.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
